title: Nothing About Sperm Whales Is Normal… Here’s Why
title_pattern: 'Nothing About [X] Is Normal… Here's Why' — absolute-negation superlative about one familiar animal + ellipsis pause + explicit promise of explanation. Template: 'Nothing About {subject} Is Normal… Here's Why'.

thumbnail.composition: Full-bleed deep-blue underwater photo of a pod of sperm whales sleeping vertically like pillars; one whale large in the right-centre foreground; a tiny diver in a red suit floats mid-frame among them. Left third darkened by a vignette/gradient to hold the text.
thumbnail.text: Four stacked left-aligned lines in heavy condensed sans: 'WE / REALLY / CAN'T' in white, 'EXPLAIN' larger in pure red.
thumbnail.colours: Monochrome deep navy/cobalt with sun-ray streaks; only accents are the red word and the red diver (colour rhyme).
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Human (~3% of frame height) vs whales filling 2/3 of frame height; the vertical sleeping posture itself is an unexplained visual anomaly.
thumbnail.why_it_works: The image is a real, strange-looking phenomenon (whales asleep standing up) that makes viewers ask 'what is that?'; the text 'We really can't explain' confesses mystery instead of claiming answers, and the title adds a different promise ('Here's why'), so thumb + title together make a gap. The tiny diver gives instant scale. Red ties the word to the human.

hook.verbatim_first_5s: (0-4s music only over deep-sea ROV footage) '3,000 m below the surface, where sunlight died an hour ago. Something is hunting.' (~4-13s)
hook.device: Cold open in media res: sensory scene-setting with a number + poetic image, then an unnamed threat ('Something is hunting'). No title, no greeting, no channel intro. Escalates with second-person body horror ('crush human bones into splinters', 'stop your heart') and a single animal's heartbeat countdown before the set-piece click reveal at 0:53.

beats.summary: Music-led cold open at 3000 m: darkness, pressure, cold; 'Something is hunting.' Whale's heart slows 60->10 bpm, 40 min breath-hold.
'Then it fires': real click recordings on black, sonar visualised, echo reveals a giant squid; fight montage.
No-VO black text cards: no one has seen the full encounter, it happens daily, 'The deepest hunt.'
Life happens in the light, sperm whales live in a vertical world; we know almost nothing; vertical sleeping pods; codas and possible language; brain 6x ours.
Divers meet whales in open blue; whale scans you inside-out; they hover, circle, respond; 'Here's what breaks you': despite slaughter they approach and try to understand us. Closes on quote card.
Sailors' fear: sea devils, Kraken; hull-knocking sounds; sucker scars birthing the giant squid myth; Essex 1820 ramming and cannibalism; Melville's Moby-Dick.

Spermaceti oil as 'liquid gold' powering industry; New England fleets; brutal hunts and learned fear; global fleets, slow reproduction, >1M killed; 1986 moratorium; partial recovery. 'We nearly erased them... but we never understood them.'
Engineering for the abyss: 300x pressure; head as sonar cannon (spermaceti acoustic lens, 230 dB vs jet 140 dB); lung collapse, flexible ribs, myoglobin; heart 60->10; largest brain on Earth.
Codas spoken as numbers (1-1-3, 4-2-1, 3-1-2); clan dialects; calves learn = culture; possible syntax; AI decoding project.

Matriarch-led families and inherited routes; whales fertilize the sea (iron -> plankton -> oxygen/carbon); whale falls feed deep ecosystems for a century; summary list 'engineers, matriarchs, hunters, teachers, navigators, living memory of the sea'.
Music-out on vertical pod, 'Thank You!' end card. No explicit CTA in VO.

pacing.avg_shot_length_note: Hard-cut detector (scene>0.3) found 225 cuts -> 5.9 s upper bound; sensitive detector (>0.12, counts dissolves and some motion) found 412 -> 3.2 s lower bound; contact sheets suggest ~4 s typical. Archival-art section holds 4-10 s per image with Ken Burns moves; hunt set-piece cuts every 1-2 s.
pacing.notes: Slow, deep-voiced documentary delivery with long music beds and deliberate silences (46 s of text cards with no VO at 1:45-2:31; 5-15 s music breathers between chapters). Many dissolves and fades to black between chapters.

techniques_worth_copying: Cold open as a mini-thriller (predator hunt) before any context; reveal the prey by echo, not by showing it first.
Silent black text-card interlude with music: one short line per card, ending on a two-word title ('The deepest hunt.').
Heartbeat/number countdowns as tension devices (60 -> 10 bpm, 40 minutes, 3,000 m, 230 dB vs 140 dB jet).
'Here's what breaks you' / 'Here's the thing' / 'Here's something no one expected' as re-hooks at every chapter turn.

Chapter order: thriller -> mystery -> emotional encounter -> myth/history -> industrial tragedy -> mechanism -> culture -> planet-scale payoff; science explanation is deferred to the 2nd half after emotional investment.
Depth-ruler infographic (water column with km ticks, whale silhouette descending) to make depth tangible.
Labelled anatomy cross-section plus dashed sound-path arrows for mechanism beats.
Comparison anchors for every big number (pressure crushes a car into a cube; 230 dB vs jet engine; whale = thousands of trees).
On-screen coda numbers (1-1-3, 4-2-1) synced to the VO reading them aloud.
Era-matched visual treatment: 3D captain's-study room and Ken Burns engravings for history, B&W pillarboxed film for 1900s, CRT-framed footage for 1980s.
Closing litany of identity nouns ('engineers, matriarchs, hunters, teachers, navigators, and the living memory of the sea').
Thumbnail: confession of mystery ('WE REALLY CAN'T EXPLAIN') vs title promise ('Here's why') — paired, not repeated.

Sonar visualiser: expanding cyan stroke rings/arcs from the head, ring lock-on around a squid silhouette, returning echo cone (SVG circles with animated r and opacity).
Squid vs whale fight as silhouette/shape animation with tentacle bezier paths, red flash overlays and camera shake.
Text-card component: black background, centered small text with fade-in/hold/fade-out timed to music, final larger title card.
Depth-ruler infographic component (km ticks, 'Ocean Surface' label, whale icon descending, scrolling camera).
Anatomy cross-section SVG of the head (spermaceti, junk/melon, cranium, jaws, muscles) with labels that draw on and dashed animated sound path; x-ray overlay highlighting lungs/heart/ribs.
Heartbeat counter / big-number callouts with comparison bars (230 dB vs 140 dB; 60 vs 10 bpm; 300x pressure).

History treatment without archival art: parchment/engraving-style SVG illustrations (hatching filters), Ken Burns pan/zoom component, sepia/B&W film-grain + flicker + pillarbox filter, CRT-frame mask, animated route lines on a stylised map.
Coda visualiser: click dots in rhythmic groups with numeric labels (1-1-3, 4-2-1, 3-1-2) synced to synthetic click audio, waveform/spectrogram strip.
Ecology diagrams: nutrient/iron particles rising to plankton layer, carbon arrows, whale-fall seafloor scene with small creature sprites.
Long-form audio: deep slow TTS (~120 wpm) with ambient drone music bed, deliberate silences, click SFX.

notes: Visuals are mostly licensed/stock nature footage (credit lines 'Courtesy - ...' bottom-left), archival paintings/engravings and B&W film, plus some CGI (sonar, anatomy, 3D study room). VO likely AI/deep-voice narration. Script says 'Earth Species Project' while showing Project CETI's website — a factual mismatch. Transcript from YouTube auto-subs (en).
